title: High-pressure separator of a CO2-to-methanol loop (illustrative state): PR + gE (MHV1) against PR with k_ij on chepta@0.6.0 and chepta@0.6.1 and chepta@0.6.2
question: At CHEPTA's illustrative separator state (CO2, H2, CO, methanol, water at 313 K and 5 MPa), what do PR + gE (MHV1) and plain PR with k_ij give through chepta@0.6.0's command line, with which parameter coverage and warnings; does 0.6.0 reproduce CHEPTA's own earlier numbers; and is SRK + gE (MHV1) still refused?
written_by: CHEPTA-Lab agent session (Claude); runs executed by this session on chepta@0.6.0

sources.note: The only source is CHEPTA's decision file (copied unchanged to upstream/). The methanol paper (medrano-garcia-2025) is deliberately not cited: none of its conditions is used.

warning_notes.note: Three gas + gas pairs (CO2 + H2, CO2 + CO, H2 + CO) have no NRTL set: g^E = 0, with a warning each. One warning says a databank NRTL set fitted at low pressure is used inside the rule, without naming the pair (the pair list shows methanol + water, fitted-zhang2019-etal, fitted at 101.3 kPa). The run does not flag the fit-quality known issues of four MHV1 sets; their fit errors are only in each pair's source text. The top-level qualifications.warnings is empty: warnings sit on the streams.

Four pairs without k_ij (k_ij = 0): CO2 + CO, H2 + methanol, H2 + water, CO + water. The H2 + CO k_ij comes from data at 68.2-88.2 K, used at 313 K. CHEPTA advises PR + gE (MHV1) above 10 bar and names four of its sets 'with a fit-quality warning'.
Refusal kept as written: CO2 + water has no NRTL parameters inside the SRK rule.

On 0.6.1 the MHV1 run carries four 'Fit quality of the MHV1 set for ...' warnings (CO2 + methanol, CO2 + water, H2 + methanol, CO + water) and a quality_warning field on those pairs in qualifications.pairs, and the databank-NRTL warning now names its pair (Methanol + Water). The three gas + gas pairs still have g^E = 0. The source ids attached to CO2 + water, H2 + methanol, CO + methanol and methanol + water are unchanged from 0.6.0; CHEPTA's coordinator calls them a naming artefact with correct data, which Lab has not verified.
Same four pairs without k_ij and the same advice as on 0.6.0.

Refusal kept as written: still NOT_AVAILABLE for CO2 + water; the message now lists the pairs fitted so far and suggests giving the pair's parameters in mixing.nrtl or using SRK with its k_ij. Lab did not try that.

New on 0.6.2: one listed extrapolation, Hydrogen + Carbon monoxide PR k_ij set (fitted at 68.2-88.2 K) used at 313 K, 224.8 K above its range, 'an extrapolation, not data'. Flash numbers unchanged. The MHV1 run lists none (empty list). No estimated pairs in any run; the SRK + gE (MHV1) refusal for CO2 + water is unchanged (NOT_AVAILABLE).

limitations: One flash at an illustrative state; not the methanol paper, not a loop, no reactor, no recycle.
Agreement with the decision file is CHEPTA against its own earlier result (a regression check), not validation.
Four MHV1 pair sets carry fit-quality known issues in CHEPTA's data; the MHV1 run on chepta@0.6.0 does not flag them; the chepta@0.6.1 run does.
chepta@0.6.2 (2026-11-13): same flash numbers and warnings as 0.6.1; the plain-PR run lists one extrapolation (H2 + CO k_ij set); no estimated pairs; SRK + gE (MHV1) still refused.

Sensitivity runs 2026-11-13 (results-chepta-0.6.2-kij0-strict/): k_ij(H2,CO) = 0 moves the outlets of the plain-PR run by at most 4e-3 relative (CO in the liquid) and leaves the PR + gE (MHV1) run identical; strictRanges true did not refuse any run and left the values unchanged. Neither run set validates the result.
